name: Chatwoot Cloud
subcategory: help desks, live chat and support knowledge
tagline: Use a managed shared inbox and website widget instead of operating Chatwoot yourself

tiers.name: Hacker
tiers.limits: Up to 2 agents, 500 conversations/month, live-chat channel only and 30-day data retention

tiers.name: Startups
tiers.limits: Unlimited conversations subject to fair use; 300 Captain AI credits/month; 1-year retention; all channels except voice
tiers.notes: Only annual per-agent pricing was published on the live Cloud page.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Unlimited conversations subject to fair use; 500 AI credits/month; voice, teams and automations; 2-year retention
tiers.notes: Only annual per-agent pricing was published on the live Cloud page.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Unlimited conversations subject to fair use; 800 AI credits/month; SSO/SAML and audit logs; 3-year retention
tiers.notes: Only annual per-agent pricing was published on the live Cloud page; video/voice support is available only at 20+ agents.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 2 agents; 500 conversations/month; live chat only; 30-day data retention
pricing.billingTerms: annual only on the published Cloud pricing page; 15-day trial
pricing.hiddenCosts: Extra Captain AI credits cost $20 per 1,000 and are non-refundable. 'Unlimited' conversations are governed by fair use; video/voice support on Enterprise requires 20+ agents.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Chatwoot Cloud, use a managed shared inbox and website widget instead of operating Chatwoot yourself. The hard boundary is managed upgrades, backups, delivery infrastructure, support, and integrations, plus channel integrations and support operations.
coreLoopDIY: Receive customer messages through a website widget, route them into a shared inbox, reply from one place, and retain a searchable conversation history.
whatYouLose: managed upgrades, backups, delivery infrastructure, support, and integrations
ongoingBurden: message delivery, webhooks, threading, identity, permissions, attachments, notifications, spam, search, uptime, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Chatwoot Cloud because support software survives because missing or misrouting one customer message is expensive and every channel behaves differently. The recurring cost buys message delivery, webhooks, threading, identity, permissions, attachments, notifications, spam, search, uptime, and retention, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Chatwoot
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source customer engagement and shared-inbox platform.

alternatives.name: Chatwoot
alternatives.desc: A proper support inbox with chat, email and a help center; free software, billable server chores.

facts.install: Docker Compose on a Linux VM, followed by environment, database, reverse-proxy and TLS configuration
facts.dataFormat: Application data in PostgreSQL, queues/cache in Redis, and attachments on local disk or S3-compatible/cloud object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: The software is the same core, but you lose Chatwoot Cloud's managed upgrades, backups, monitoring and incident response.
facts.setupBlocker: Provisioning a Linux server and correctly wiring DNS/TLS, SMTP, PostgreSQL/Redis and storage

alternatives.name: HubSpot Free CRM
alternatives.desc: A two-seat shared inbox and live chat bolted to a CRM; free until the limits become colleagues.

facts.install: Hosted signup, then connect a team inbox/email and add the website tracking or chat-widget code
facts.dataFormat: CRM contacts and conversation history in HubSpot's cloud; records export to spreadsheet files and conversations are available through its API
facts.gapVsPaid: It is capped at two users and replaces Chatwoot's omnichannel support model with a CRM-centric inbox.
facts.setupBlocker: Connecting and verifying the shared email inbox and website domain

alternatives.name: tawk.to
alternatives.desc: Live chat, tickets and a knowledge base for zero dollars; the little badge is how the arithmetic survives.

facts.install: Hosted signup, then paste the generated JavaScript widget or install a CMS plugin
facts.dataFormat: Chats, tickets and contacts in tawk.to's cloud account; chat and ticket exports are JSON
facts.gapVsPaid: You accept vendor branding and less control over inbox workflows and data than Chatwoot Cloud.
facts.setupBlocker: Access to edit the website or install its CMS plugin

alternatives.name: HubSpot Free Help Desk
alternatives.desc: A hosted shared inbox, live chat, and ticket queue for two users; the knowledge base lives upstairs.

facts.install: Hosted signup, then connect a team inbox/email and add the website tracking or chat-widget code
facts.dataFormat: CRM records, tickets and conversation history in HubSpot's cloud; records export to spreadsheet files and conversations are available through its API
facts.gapVsPaid: The two-user free ceiling and shallower support automation make it a small-team stopgap rather than an equivalent managed inbox.
facts.setupBlocker: Connecting and verifying the shared email inbox and website domain

alternatives.name: Odoo Helpdesk One App Free
alternatives.desc: A real hosted ticket desk for unlimited users, as long as Helpdesk is your one free Odoo app.

facts.install: Hosted Odoo Online signup with Helpdesk selected as the single free app
facts.dataFormat: An Odoo Online PostgreSQL database in Odoo's cloud, with record exports and downloadable ZIP database backups
facts.gapVsPaid: The one-app-free rule and Odoo-wide workflow model are less focused than Chatwoot Cloud's support inbox.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Startups plan and a small-team shared inbox DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Chatwoot Cloud in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, WebSockets, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: receive customer messages through a website widget, route them into a shared inbox, reply from one place, and retain a searchable conversation history.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement one workspace, agents, contacts, inboxes, conversations, messages, labels, and assignment.
Provide a website chat widget with reconnect, unread counts, file limits, and clear availability state.
Create a shared inbox with filters, collision warnings, notes, canned replies, and searchable history.
Add email notifications, browser notifications, and an immutable assignment and status log.
Implement spam controls, attachment scanning hooks, retention settings, export, and contact deletion.
Ship Docker Compose, backups, health checks, migrations, and a documented admin recovery flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out many social and messaging channels.
Deliberately leave out AI agents trained on proprietary support data.
Deliberately leave out enterprise workforce management, SSO, and compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
